title: Downtime triage and safe ratios
scenario: Pelvaris Mill is triaging 24 fictitious downtime events. Some events lose zero units, which is a valid measurement rather than missing data. Supervisors need duration bands and cost-per-lost-unit decisions that explain zero-denominator cases.

lesson.intro: Ordered decision rules and safe error handling keep a report readable. Do not convert every error into zero: zero cost and an undefined cost-per-unit ratio mean different things.

functions.name: IFS
functions.purpose: Return the result for the first true condition.
functions.arguments: Each test is paired with its result; later test/result pairs are optional.
functions.mistake: Put narrower conditions first; TRUE at the end supplies a catch-all outcome.

functions.name: IFERROR
functions.purpose: Use a stated fallback if an expression produces an Excel error.
functions.arguments: value is the calculation; value_if_error is returned only when that calculation errors.
functions.useCase: Explain an undefined ratio without breaking a dashboard.
functions.mistake: IFERROR also hides unexpected errors; verify references before adding a fallback.

lesson.combine: Reuse ROUND for currency-per-unit outputs and IF for a threshold decision. IFS assigns duration labels in increasing upper-bound order. IFERROR belongs outside the entire ratio calculation or ratio-based decision. A zero-denominator fallback should remain text, not a misleading number.

tasks.prompt: Classify the first event’s Duration_min as Short for at most 10 minutes, Medium for more than 10 through 30 minutes, or Long for more than 30 minutes.
For the first six events, calculate Labor_cost_CAD per Units_lost, rounded to two decimals. Return No lost units when the ratio is undefined. Keep dataset order.
For the first six events, classify Duration_min as Critical for at least 45 minutes, Priority for at least 20 but less than 45, otherwise Routine. Keep dataset order.
For the first eight events, return Review when the unrounded Labor_cost_CAD per Units_lost exceeds 15, otherwise Accept. Return No loss when the ratio is undefined. Keep dataset order.

bonus.prompt: Calculate overall labour cost per lost unit across all 24 events, rounded to two decimals. Include labour cost from zero-loss events in the total cost.

columns.name: Units_lost
columns.description: Nonnegative units lost; zero is a valid observed result.

columns.name: Labor_cost_CAD
columns.description: Event labour recovery cost, Canadian dollars.
